solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: something declared is spoken out, so the word for the service is taken by its sound

parts.note: a rite is a religious service or ceremony

explanation.surface: Someone announces that the church service was done correctly.
explanation.definitionFit: Right and proper are synonyms meaning correct or fitting, as in the right way to behave.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to sway or jolt violently
second meaning: a dependable person you can lean on

explanation.surface: A reliable person is shaken by events.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to sway or unsettle; as a noun it is a steadfast, dependable supporter.

indicators.note: about means around, so the chatter word wraps itself around the other letter

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: People gossip about the correct outfit to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside GAB, after its first two letters, giving GA-R-B.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is a slightly formal or literary word for clothing or dress of a particular kind.

clue.text: Orange colour with green I mixed

indicators.note: mixed letters are stirred up and laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: Mixing green paint into a tin to get an orange shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orange colour' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just Orange, the fruit; colour gives TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small, loose-skinned citrus fruit, a kind of orange.

indicators.note: in places one word inside another, here the thinking word inside the sleeping place

explanation.surface: A sailor lies in a bunk on board ship, thinking things over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' looks like it sets the scene on a ship; it means confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at sea is bewildered or puzzled, which is exactly what bemused means.

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone resentful because a piece of their theory was challenged.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter describes feeling angry and hurt at unfair treatment, the same as resentful.

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word turns it upside down so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a dam is a barrier across a river

explanation.surface: It would be foolish to build a barrier higher.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad means foolish or lacking reason, so it shares the sense of senseless.

clue.text: Guard posted in front of queue with head down

indicators.note: the head of the word drops down to the bottom, so its first letter moves to the end

explanation.surface: A guard is stationed at the front of a queue, head bowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In front of' just places SENT before the second piece in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentinel is a soldier or guard posted to keep watch.

clue.text: Party with friend keeping in control

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the friend word surrounds the small word

explanation.surface: At a party, a friend keeps everyone in line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests a political party, but here it is a social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: To dominate is to have power over or control something, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Expression of surprise about alien crown

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at the sight of an alien wearing a crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a container signal but here simply gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronet is a small crown, worn by nobility below the rank of monarch.

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front, so the word is read right to left

explanation.surface: Material that was dug up after some thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a hard-wearing cotton cloth, a material used for jeans.

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters end up in a mess

explanation.surface: Dull workouts that leave you badly strained.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian as an adjective means dull and uninspired, a synonym of boring.

clue.text: Note part of flower, botanist's ultimate evidence

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
the stamen is the pollen-bearing part of a flower

indicators.note: ultimate means final, so only the closing letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A botanist's notes on part of a flower serve as final evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament is proof or evidence of something, as in a testament to their skill.

parts.note: a traffic jam is a hold-up
bore is the past tense of bear, to tolerate
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Delays put up with on the way to an English festival.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamboree is a large celebration or gathering, especially of Scouts, so a kind of festival.

indicators.note: badly means in a poor state, so the letters are disordered
losing means giving up, so a letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A corrupt manufacturer behaves badly and wastes time.
explanation.definitionFit: A producer is one who makes goods, the same as a manufacturer.

clue.text: Run into trouble, facing appeal that's skilful

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the single letter goes within the trouble word

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Running into difficulty while making an appeal that's cleverly done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facing' puts IT after A-R-DO. IT for appeal is an old slang sense: charm or sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means clever and deft with the hands or mind, a synonym of skilful.

parts.note: a scent is a trail followed by a hound

explanation.surface: Following a trail up a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'on' means after: the trail comes after the a.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is an upward climb or incline, so a slope that rises.

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the prediction word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: a bet is a prediction of the outcome
ill means bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: A forecast that the lodgings would be poor.
explanation.definitionFit: A billet is lodging, especially quarters for soldiers in a private house.

clue.text: Cage bird in capital city right after move

parts.note: to budge is to move slightly
Riga is the capital of Latvia
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A caged bird in a capital is let out after being moved.
explanation.walkthrough: Riga is the capital of Latvia; 'in' only links the bird to its wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A budgerigar is a small Australian parakeet, commonly kept as a pet in a cage.

clue.text: Bean curd contributing to hint of umami

indicators.note: the answer contributes letters to a longer phrase, so it lies within the following words

parts.note: found across the end of hint, of, and the start of umami

explanation.surface: Bean curd adds a touch of savoury umami flavour to a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hint of umami' looks like a first-letter instruction, but it is the phrase hiding the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tofu is curd made from soya milk, so it is bean curd by its usual English description.

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece holds the other up from beneath, so it is written lower down

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A church backing a well-liked policy.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supporting' puts CH beneath IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is a unit of length, so a measure.

clue.text: Step back after end of your summary

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is taken
back means going backwards, so the step word is read from right to left

explanation.surface: Stepping back at the end to give an overview.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the reversed step after the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Recap is short for recapitulation, a brief summary of what has been said.

clue.text: Turnover perhaps that is under pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the preceding piece below the following one

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure
i.e. is the abbreviation of Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: A business's turnover is put under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnover' looks like business income but is a folded pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnover is a folded pastry with a filling, an example of a pie; perhaps flags the example.

indicators.note: something shattered is broken into pieces, which are put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: Lazy and exhausted, you should take a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shattered' is British slang for exhausted, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-down is a short rest lying on a bed or sofa.

indicators.note: out suggests letters spilt from their usual places, to be laid down differently

explanation.surface: A grave profit has been laid out.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means sincere and serious in intention or manner.

indicators.note: not here means without, so a letter is left out of the next piece

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Something is not difficult, even if it seems baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not hard' looks like a definition meaning easy, which contradicts the answer; it actually removes H.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough problem is a hard one to solve, so tough here means puzzling or difficult.
